newsitem.title: CANADA: TENNIS-SAWAMATSU UPSETS MAJOLI AT CANADIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAWAMATSU UPSETS MAJOLI AT CANADIAN OPEN.

text.p: Unseeded Naoko Sawamatsu of Japan ousted second-seeded French Open champion Iva Majoli of Croatia 7-5 6-7 (5-7) 6-1 in second-round play in the $926,250 Canadian Open on Wednesday.

"She played well," the fourth-ranked Majoli said a day after a raucous birthday celebration, "but my legs were heavy because I'd taken 10 days off. I can't say that I played that bad for my first match since Wimbledon."
Top-seeded Monica Seles won her third-round match by beating 16th-seeded Sabine Appelmans of Belgium 6-3 7-5.
The third-ranked Seles will have Thursday off before meeting the winner of a match between sixth-seeded Mary Pierce of France and qualifier Rita Grande of Italy in the quarter-finals on Friday.

Among other seeded players advancing to the round of 16 were third seed Amanda Coetzer of South Africa, a 4-6 6-4 6-2 winner over qualifier Nathalie Dechy of France, fourth-seeded American Lindsay Davenport 6-2 7-6 (8-6) over Ai Sugiyama of Japan and fifth seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, 6-2 6-1 over American Anne Miller.
Tenth-seeded American Mary Joe Fernandez defeated compatriot Nicole Arendt 6-4, 6-2 and another all-American confrontation was won by 11th-seeded Kimberly Po, 6-3 6-2 over unseeded Jennifer Capriati.
"This definitely wasn't Jennifer's best match," said the 17th-ranked Po. "She missed a lot but it really wasn't our best tennis because it was pretty windy."

"I felt a lack of stamina, a lack of fitness out there," said the 33rd-ranked Capriati, playing her second match in as many days after returning from three months off due to an ankle injury. "I think that's just from not playing and from yesterday" when she scored a 6-3 6-4 win over 41st-ranked Silvia Farina of Italy.

The 52nd-ranked Sawamatsu, often thought of as a counter-puncher, hit 37 winners in the two-hour, 19-minute match against Majoli. That was just three fewer winners than Majoli, who had celebrated her 20th birthday with several other players on Tuesday evening.
The players treated Majoli to an "adults only" performance by a local dancer who dressed as a member of a law enforcement brigade sent to "arrest" the birthday girl.
After losing the second set on a very close call that she mildly protested, Sawamatsu recomposed herself for the final set.
"At the end of the second set," said the 24-year-old from Tokyo, "I felt very tired. But when I looked at Majoli she looked more tired than me. That's why my mental confidence came back again."
"She was moving well amd made so many winners that I had to work really hard for every point," Majoli said. "In the third set, my legs were heavy and I just wanted to finish the point soon."
"I was really tired," Seles said after beating the 20th-ranked Appelmans. "Because I've been playing so much tennis." This is her fourth tournament in as many weeks.
"But when I needed it, I think I played some good tennis on the key points. It was good to know I had that in me."
